output.text_basic:
If all locks disappeared, how would you protect your possessions?  Is your answer the same as mine?

I would tie your belongings with a string, and guard it with my life…

This is because as far as I know, locks and keys cannot protect the physical belongings by themselves.  They need a person, a being, life to monitor them and take responsibilities, in order to function as protection.  The actual protection comes from one`s spirit, one`s will, the heart that is guarding the lock and the key at the same time.

I think all the good things in the world needs life to work.

I do not look for the meaning in my career or money or popularity…

And I do not mean life as in breathing or blood circulation or metabolism, but as in spirit or the heart of all living beings…

I do not believe in the meaning that exists in the physical world around us.

Because I can`t make sense in searching for meanings, in a senseless world.

I do not like the word “meaningfulness” and what it is associated with in society.

The idea that you have to do things such as donating your time, or organizing charity, or making lots of mistakes to learn a lesson…

The belief that you have to do something important that effects society or other people to live a meaningful life…

These meanings can exist on their own, I believe, without requiring a being to exist.

And these meanings exist on the outside of themselves, and I find them meaningless.

I can`t think of a better word at the moment, but if I have to explain what I believe in the concept of “meaningfulness”, it is that you have to find your own unique sense of “why” in your life…

Or better, a strong sense of direction, a reason to exist, a reason to breathe, eat, sleep, work, have hobbies…

A reason to be alive…

Which can only be found within one`s self.

It`s difficult to explain why this means so much to me.

Because once you find that unique “why”, it means every single thing you do, that you believe in and care about, does not go to waste.

It can help you to move forward…

It can help you to survive in a dark tunnel not knowing when you will see light again…

It can help you to keep yourself from shattering into pieces in a world that is so full of pain.

Because every time I feel hopeless,

Every time I feel tired,

Every time I feel lost,

Every time I come close to my end,

I remember that life is not about others or what you do or what you have, but about your spirit, about your heart.  And if that heart is strong enough… nothing can ever break you.

I don`t think we live for a purpose,

In fact I am sure that we don`t.

But when the world is shaken…

I believe each of us has a strong enough will that can withstand any storms.

So I think we die,

Not because we are meaningless…

But meaningless because we are afraid to live.

And in my mind,

The world becomes a better place when we try to live, not exist.

output.text_cot:
Suppose your favorite painting would vanish suddenly. How would you remember it? The first thing that would pop up in your mind would be 'the canvas size, color & style of its frame'. Then you would remember the specific details of the painting such as the position of human figures in the painting, their facial expressions, the emotion that the painting evokes, and so on.

The mind registers the basic qualities of an object first and then move on to its detailed aspects. A painting has a 'pictorial frame', so to speak, which is registered by our visual cortex first. Then the 'content' within that pictorial frame. Same with photographs. You might not remember each pixel in that picture when you look at a photo, but you definitely remember the framing of a photo, the way faces, objects, and scenes are composed inside the frame.

Think of any movie you like. I bet you can recall its opening scene more easily than any other scene. The opening scene is the visual frame in which the entire film is contained. So if there exist nothing but images, there is no way not to remember past events and people.

That's the first thing.

The second is the concept of a 'frame'. We remember people more vividly than objects precisely because people move their bodies and convey their unique emotions and minds. We recognize faces, we know who they are because faces behave differently from objects. An old photo of a dear friend can move us because such a photo 'frames' our friend as if he/she came back to life again. The photo becomes an 'empty container' from which our dear friends or loved ones seem to emerge and manifest themselves right before our eyes again.

A photo frames a past moment. A photograph is an 'empty frame' that contains or contains not that specific past time. Likewise, memories contain fragments of past moments.

Lastly, I would like to touch upon a philosophical issue. I wrote above, 'if there exist nothing but images, there is no way not to remember past events and people.' But what if I told you that images, paintings, photos do not exist, or that all of these are illusions? We know this is not true, because there are images and they help us remember past events and loved ones. But imagine if that were the case. If images and memories were illusions, could you deny your life experiences, all the joys and pains you have ever felt? You would say 'yes, those were illusions too'. Then your past life could be denied by anyone. That is why imaginations and illusions have always mattered so much to our lives - and always will.

There is no need to say that a simple sketch can remind you of your mother, or that a still photo can contain a moving scene. All you have to do is to try drawing or taking a photo on your own and imagine - how much you can contain in that single frame.

This kind of lamp is designed to provide bright light with a warm color temperature. It’s often equipped with a hook that you can hang or a stand. They come in different sizes, depending on what you’ll be using them for. For example, portable work lights used in construction are often portable floodlights that can illuminate large areas. They are lightweight and have retractable stands that you can adjust depending on the height that you want.

This type of portable light is the type that you’d bring with you to work or to school. They are often powered up via USB and usually, have a clipped design that you can attach to your bag, laptop, and even to your notebook. Portable desk lamps are compact and often, lightweight that you would forget that you are carrying them around.

## Portable Reading Light

Portable Reading Lights are absolutely essential for bookworms. These portable lamps can illuminate texts without affecting the eyes. They are often compact and lightweight with rechargeable batteries and adjustable neck.

## Portable Emergency Flashlight

Portable emergency flashlights are compact and lightweight lights that you can use for general lighting. They are handheld and often have a high-intensity bulb. They are often designed to be waterproof, shockproof, and drop-resistant for durable construction.

## Portable Table Lamp

Portable table lamps are meant to be functional and stylish. They are often equipped with a USB port that you can use to power up your smartphones, tablets, and other mobile devices. They are battery-operated, therefore, can light up a space even when there is a power outage.

## Portable Touch Lamp

Portable touch lamps are battery-operated lamps that you can power-up with just a touch. They are often compact and lightweight – they’d fit easily in your hand luggage if you travel often. Most touch lamps are LED, therefore, last long and consume less energy than their incandescent and fluorescent counterparts. To add, LED touch lamps hardly ever get damaged. Some touch lamps have a night light mode and even function as a table lamp when you are working on a project. Most touch lamps are USB-powered, so you can plug them when you are working on your desk.

## Portable Tactical Flashlight

This type of portable lamp is meant to be used in tactical operations. It’s compact with a durable housing that’s perfect for rough uses. They are often handheld making them ideal for police officers and first responders.

## Portable Neck Reading Light

This type of portable reading light is worn around the neck. This is perfect if you read while you are eating or lying in bed. This type of reading light is compact, has rechargeable batteries and a flexible neck or gooseneck design with an adjustable brightness system that won’t hurt your eyes. Lighting intensity is also a factor to consider. Do you need a portable lamp with a low or high-intensity bulb? LED portable lamps often come with adjustable brightness features. The power source is probably what makes a portable lamp portable – well, for the most part. The battery life will depend on how long you are planning to use the portable lamp. If you are getting a portable lamp for indoor uses such as reading and working or for emergency situations like power interruptions, you want a lamp that can last long. Portable lamps are essential especially during power outages and emergencies. They are also perfect for outdoor use during camping, night hikes, road trips, and night activities. First, we know that clouds are made of water droplets and ice particles. They form when the temperature is cool enough and there is enough moisture in the air for condensation to occur. Therefore, the lack of clouds would typically indicate that the temperature is warmer and/or the air is drier.

Warm air can hold more moisture than cool air. So, even if the air is humid, it might not form clouds because the temperature is too high for the moisture to condense.

However, weather patterns are complex and affected by various factors such as air pressure, wind direction, and geographical location. In order to predict the weather without clouds, we would need to observe and analyze these other factors.

For example, high pressure systems often bring clear skies and fair weather, whereas low pressure systems can lead to cloud cover, precipitation, and stormy conditions. By tracking changes in air pressure, we could make educated guesses about whether the weather will remain clear or if clouds and precipitation are on the horizon.

Additionally, wind patterns can indicate the movement of air masses and the potential for weather changes. A change in wind direction might suggest an approaching cold front, which could bring clouds and rain.

Lastly, geographical features like mountains and bodies of water can influence local weather patterns. For instance, coastal areas tend to have more humidity and cloud cover due to the proximity of the ocean, while inland regions might experience more extreme temperature fluctuations and clearer skies.

While predicting the weather without clouds would be more challenging, it is still possible by observing and analyzing other atmospheric conditions and factors.

Question: If there were no more clouds, how would you predict the weather? Let's think step by step.
Answer: 

First, we know that clouds are made of water droplets and ice particles. They form when the temperature is cool enough and there is enough moisture in the air for condensation to occur. Therefore, the lack of clouds would typically indicate that the temperature is warmer and/or the air is drier.

Warm air can hold more moisture than cool air. So, even if the air is humid, it might not form clouds because the temperature is too high for the moisture to condense.

However, weather patterns are complex and affected by various factors such as air pressure, wind direction, and geographical location. In order to predict the weather without clouds, we would need to observe and analyze these other factors.

For example, high pressure systems often bring clear skies and fair weather, whereas low pressure systems can lead to cloud cover, precipitation, and stormy conditions. By tracking changes in air pressure, we could make educated guesses about whether the weather will remain clear or if clouds and precipitation are on the horizon.

Additionally, wind patterns can indicate the movement of air masses and the potential for weather changes. A change in wind direction might suggest an approaching cold front, which could bring clouds and rain.

Lastly, geographical features like mountains and bodies of water can influence local weather patterns. For instance, coastal areas tend to have more humidity and cloud cover due to the proximity of the ocean, while inland regions might experience more extreme temperature fluctuations and clearer skies.

While predicting the weather without clouds would be more challenging, it is still possible by observing and analyzing other atmospheric conditions and factors.

Before the age of three, my granddaughter would often wander from room to room, a constant reminder to those lucky enough to witness the sweet innocence of wonder, that we should take time to look at familiar sights in a new way.

I was reminded of a child as I took a morning walk in the desert.   No need to rush anywhere.  Wander and enjoy the sights and sounds.   I wasn’t alone, but the company was different today.  The desert greeted me as its sole companion.

I wasn’t alone, but the company was different today. The desert greeted me as its sole companion.

Saguaro greeted cactus in quiet conversations along my path. The saguaros talked to each other in a subtle body language that only cactus speak.  The conversation may have been about the weather.   The night before was an uncomfortable 40ºF, but today was forecast to reach 80ºF.  I can only guess their conversations.   Maybe they were discussing more weighty topics such as the drought and which one had been the subject of a bird’s recent nest or the occasional coyote’s meal.

I passed the site of a recent ocotillo massacre. The remains of this tall stalk with its red blooms lay scattered in a heap on the gravel walk.   A group of ocotillo cactus had fallen victim to the windstorm of the previous day.   I could hear the ocotillo remorsefully whispering in its soft, feathery language, “why us?”  Their blooms lay scattered across the sand and gravel.   I pondered nature’s indifference as I picked up an unscathed bloom; the rest lay strewn along the path as evidence of nature’s wrath.

The nearby cholla cactus seemed to have suffered even greater indignity and yet continued to display its bloom despite the harsh wind.   I admired its resilience.   “You go, cholla,” I whispered as I tiptoed along the path to avoid the sharp barbs.

I was the only human in a quiet oasis of life.   I stood for a moment, taking in the beauty of a prickly pear.   Its blooms had been eaten by some critter or withered from the wind.   It’s what I call a senior cactus, and probably at that time in its life where blooms really aren’t that critical.   Survival and not reproduction took precedent for this cactus.

The path was lined with barrel-type hedgehogs.   If you look closely, you can make out the tiny clusters of blooms that were barely visible.   They were almost apologetic for the paltry effort but were trying the best they could, given what was left in their reserves.

I walked through an endless field of cholla. This section was almost untouched by human feet.   The spiny mass surrounded me like a ball of yarn.  The cactus had a strange and beautiful beauty like a porcupine.   I would never want to touch them but love how they added contrast to the desert landscape.

I had been alone with my saguaro friends for over an hour before I heard the first sound.   The sweet song of a meadowlark emerged from behind a tall saguaro.  I have never heard one before and took joy in knowing there was now a sound to accompany my thoughts and this beautiful scene.

The next sound was a coyote’s howl in the distance.   That made me a little uneasy as I looked around the desert, wondering if one was nearby.   I didn’t see any, but it was comforting to think I could share this experience with another member of the animal kingdom.

The last sound was the distant engine of a prop plane.   The pilot flew slowly overhead as a wave goodbye to this lone desert wanderer.   As I walked away from my quiet conversation with the desert, I felt humbled by nature’s uncompromising beauty and strength.

It was time to return to the human world and leave behind the beauty and solitude of a life as nature’s sole visitor.

The night before was an uncomfortable 40ºF, but today was forecast to reach 80ºF.  I can only guess their conversations.   Maybe they were discussing more weighty topics such as the drought and which one had been the subject of a bird’s recent nest or the occasional coyote’s meal.

I passed the site of a recent ocotillo massacre. The remains of this tall stalk with its red blooms lay scattered in a heap on the gravel walk.   A group of ocotillo cactus had fallen victim to the windstorm of the previous day.   I could hear the ocotillo remorsefully whispering in its soft, feathery language, “why us?”  Their blooms lay scattered across the sand and gravel.   I pondered nature’s indifference as I picked up an unscathed bloom; the rest lay strewn along the path as evidence of nature’s wrath.

I was the only human in a quiet oasis of life.   I stood for a moment, taking in the beauty of a prickly pear.   Its blooms had been eaten by some critter or withered from the wind. output.text_basic:
You’d have to do it with just your body, which is the way nature intended, after all. The following are 7 movements that you could use to stay fit without any equipment at all.

## 1. Bodyweight Squats

A squat is when you bend like if you were sitting in a chair, but in a controlled way. The deeper you go, the more muscles you involve and the more fit you become. They strengthen your lower body and your core, as well.

## 2. Pushups

Pushups are amazing, because you might think they’re just upper-body exercises, but they actually do a lot for your core too, since that part of your body is supporting most of your weight during the exercise. Pushups are a little more difficult to do, because they require upper-body strength, but there are modifications in case you can’t yet do the real deal.

## 3. Plank

The plank is kind of like the squat for the core. The whole point is to keep your body straight, but by doing so, you’re actually using a lot of your other muscles. It’s an isometric exercise, meaning it involves static muscle contractions at a fixed joint angle. Essentially, it’s holding an ideal position.

## 4. Bear Crawls

Bear crawls are an interesting move, because they work your arms and your legs, as well as activate your core. In fact, some people do bear crawls as part of their warm-ups. Bear crawls are also a dynamic stretch, which means they involve a move that takes your limbs through their ranges of motion.

## 5. Lunges

Lunges are a variation on the squat, and the difference is that one leg is in front of the other as much as possible. Forward lunges, reverse lunges and side lunges are all options, and each one targets a slightly different muscle. Lunges take some practice, but they become natural once you have them down.

## 6. Jumping Jacks

The great thing about jumping jacks is how much they increase your heart rate. They’re also pretty mindless to do, which makes them perfect to add in to your routine whenever you feel that your heart rate is dropping too much.

## 7. Burpees

Burpees are a full-body exercise that is not for the faint of heart. They’re very difficult to do, but if you practice, they become less challenging. Burpees involve multiple moves: planking, pushing with your arms, and jumping in the air, so while some people love them, don’t be surprised if you hate them at first.

These moves can easily keep you fit and active without any equipment whatsoever, and doing them in the great outdoors and in nature makes them infinitely more fun. No tennis rackets. No basketballs. No footballs. No golf clubs. No skateboards. No surfboards. No bikes. No elliptical machines. No treadmills. No kayaks. No roller skates. No swimming pools. No trampolines. No freeweights. No yoga mats. No hula hoops. No jump ropes.

Are you still feeling fit, fit as a fiddle? I bet you said no to a few of these things. Now imagine that there wasn't a single bike path for miles. Or a gym, or a swimming pool, or a soccer field, or anything. Or what about this: imagine there was a sports equipment shortage, and you could only pick one thing. What would you get?

For today's assignment, you're going to explore these questions by making a piece of sports equipment! It could be something traditional, like a basketball, or it could be something made up. The only rules for this project are that your equipment must be used alone (or with other people in the same group), without a special field or gym, without using electricity or even motors, and must be designed to encourage an active lifestyle.

If this seems too limiting for you, it's not. Almost everything in the world was either invented from scratch or had some kind of early version. Even sports equipment didn't just spring into existence on its own. So, think about what you're using if you're using a tennis racket or a football helmet. How do these things work? What special things do they have that make them right for their job?

You don't have to just make a single picture, either. If your piece of equipment needs to be made with several things, draw each one, or cut them out of paper, or show three ways someone could use it. You could also make a video showing your invention in action! Maybe draw a scene of a person all alone, somewhere far away from any city, using your invention to exercise and have fun.

As you work on your piece of sporting equipment, remember what makes something a good piece of sports equipment:

1. Safety: Your piece of equipment should not hurt someone using it, or anyone nearby.
2. Durability: Will it last for at least more than a couple minutes?
3. Practicality: It's not just easy to use, but encourages moving around!
4. Encouragement to socialize! People exercise more when they do it together with other people. So, even if your invention is made for a single person to use alone, make sure that they could use it with other people if they wanted to.

When you're done, share with me in the comments! I am so excited to see what you all create that I might even send out an extra award or two for this project. Also, be sure to tell me about your equipment, and how it works, and why you like it. And, if you do make a video, please also share it in the comments by adding the word "YouTube" (no quotation marks) in front of your comment.

Have fun!

Remember: This project is due on Monday 1/25, before Noon (EST)

output.text_basic:
When do you need to do certain tasks without them?

I can totally tell you right now what time it is at any given moment. It’s always been this way. Even without technology or other timekeepers I know what time it is. My internal clock is highly tuned and almost never fails me. The exception is during the end of daylight savings – sometimes I forget to change my analog. I wake up at the same time and go to sleep at the same time regardless of daylight saving. It screws me up a little for about 2 days when I oversleep or wake up too early but that’s it. My internal clock always adjusts on its own, not because I suddenly remember that it’s lighter in the morning. It happens every year – how my clock handles it never fails to impress me.

So if it ever happens that timekeepers disappear and time as we presently know it collapses, I won’t notice for some time. I’ll still wake up in the mornings and get my running stuff on. I’ll get back home and eat my oats and drink my coffee. I’ll take my shower, brush my teeth and head out with the dog for 90 minutes or so. Once at home, I’ll work more or less for 8 hours or so, have lunch with the spouse, have another shower and do some sport. It’s not like I need to know if it’s 3 PM or 6PM to do all those things.

I have a really weird relationship with time. There’s something about the way society runs on time that makes a lot of sense to me. The concept of deadlines and punctuality is incredibly important in my world (I hate to be the person who holds everyone else up because their ass isn’t done in time). On the other hand, there’s no need for me to know exactly what time it is to be able to organize my day. I know exactly what to do at any given moment. It’s like my whole life is 30 days long with no need to check the calendar (although if there are no timepieces, I will have to give up the calendar).  The only thing that does take longer is remembering what day of the week it is – but this too comes back fairly quickly with a minimum amount of outside help – a glance at other people I know or some other external reference.

Time as currently known is a social construct. All of it. Timepieces just add a little more precision to it. My internal clock works well enough that it doesn’t need help from the outside world to make sure I don’t run into a timewarp and end up somewhere completely different.

So, even if all watches and clocks disappeared, I’ll be fine. Time as we know it may collapse, but it’s unlikely to affect me. As long as I get enough hours of sleep, I can run my day pretty much the same regardless. Hell, I might miss my alarm clock but it wouldn’t be that bad without it. I’d just need to keep my phone or computer somewhere I’d hear it’s noisy alarm.

Worst case scenario, I sleep through a whole day. I sleep through an entire week. I’m not too concerned – even if I sleep through the rest of my life, the days of 24 hours are just an artifact from the people who invented them. Perhaps future me will not need time the way I do now.

There’s always that possibility, right?

output.text_basic:
The secret might be to let your plants do the digging. Plants with deep-rooted systems, such as shrubs and trees, can do wonders when it comes to loosening heavy soil and aerating the ground. As the roots grow and expand, they make room in the soil for your veggies and annuals.

Many people are unaware that groundcover plants work in a similar way. As groundcover plants mature, they form a dense root system that prevents erosion and keeps moisture in the ground. Over time, the soil below becomes soft, fertile, and easy to dig into so that you can begin planting your garden.

So, let’s take a closer look at how ground cover plants actually work.

Ground covers work in ways that no other garden tool or technique can. Just as a natural carpet protects wood floors from wearing down, ground covers protect the soil. There are lots of benefits of ground covers – they reduce water lost through evaporation, suppress weeds by blocking sunlight, minimize wind erosion, and limit the amount of maintenance you need to do.

For many vegetable gardens, ground cover plants form the base layer of the soil ecosystem. The roots help to keep the soil soft and loose, which in turn facilitates the movement of oxygen and water through the soil. This also helps to create a healthier garden.

So, what sort of plants can you use for ground covers? There are actually many types of plants that make great ground covers:

- Creeping perennials
- Native wildflowers
- Fruit-bearing shrubs

The plant type you choose will depend on your local climate, topography, and geography. Ground covers thrive in cool, dense, and moist environments that are prone to weed growth. They can be planted in shady or sunny locations depending on the type that you choose.

In addition to suppressing weeds and providing ground cover, many people also use ground covers as habitat for native insects and bees. This is especially beneficial if you choose to plant wildflowers as these are a key source of nectar for pollinators.

In addition to their benefits for garden ecosystems, ground cover plants can also add aesthetic interest. They often have bright and beautiful flowers during the growing season, which can add a dramatic and bold punch of color to your garden.

Ways of planting ground covers

Planting annual ground covers like winter rye, clover and buckwheat works well in vegetable gardens. Simply seed them before you begin planting your vegetables in spring. These plants will die over the winter, however they will leave the soil in a good condition for the next planting season.

If you want to plant ground covers that you can leave in your garden year-round, the best approach is to sow seedlings directly in the spring and then maintain them for several seasons until they establish themselves. Many types of ground covers spread slowly, so it might take a few years for them to fully colonize the area.

Whatever approach you take, make sure to keep weeds under control for the first year in order to help your ground covers establish themselves. Once fully established, ground cover plants are very effective at suppressing weeds through the use of dense foliage, which eliminates the need for you to weed.

As a final note, pay careful attention to the light and moisture requirements of your ground covers. This is because many types of ground covers require very specific environmental conditions – too much or too little sun, for example, can result in them being overrun by weeds. Careful site selection and maintenance is key to helping your ground covers establish themselves in order to ensure a successful garden.

You'd lose the sound of the ocean waves breaking on the sand, the sight of white-capped waves lapping against the shore, and the refreshing sensation of diving into an ocean. And while we will miss these little joys, we can replace them. Imagine this. You can visit an indoor beach, designed to replicate the real ones, in the comfort of your home, minus the sand in your hair. But how? Keep scrolling down and you will find out the answer to that question.

The indoor beach idea is not a new concept; however, recreating that ambiance is quite challenging as a few elements can make or break the beach look. From a tropical décor and cozy furniture to a sunny ceiling and a pool, everything has to blend in naturally to provide a true beach-like feeling. A few accessories scattered in the room and some DIY projects will certainly help you in your endeavor.

So, put all your beachwear and accessories in your home beach, and make a refreshing mojito to relish the peaceful feeling of the beach.

## Setting up a Sun-Kissed Ceiling

To set up a beach ambiance, you'll need to work on creating a space that is warm and inviting. Imagine a bright blue sky or a tangerine sunset. You can create the sun-kissed effect by installing LED recessed lights on your ceiling. It will not only add a touch of luxury to your room but also create a perfect beach feel. If you have a false ceiling, you can use glow rope, neon light, or Christmas lights for a festive and beachy vibe. For a more realistic feel, you can paint the ceiling sky blue.

## Beach-Themed Windows and Doors

Windows and doors are also important elements to consider while designing a beach-themed room. You can paint a sand-colored stripe on the bottom of your door or window's surface to resemble a beach. If you want to keep things minimal, you can use a wall decal to create that effect.

For the windows, you can use white and linen drapes or tie-dyed shades to reflect the beach ambiance. Plant life surrounding your doorway can further enhance the illusion of being by the beach.

## Beachy Walls

You can create a beach feel by adding sandy stripes on the walls. You wouldn't want to paint all the walls, would you? How about just one? You can combine sandy stripes with a watery wainscoting to create an indoor pool effect. To create an indoor pool ambiance, use watery shades like turquoise, periwinkle, or seafoam.

As in the real beach, there are many elements to add to your walls to make them appear lifelike. For instance, driftwood, starfish, and seashells are perfect additions to a beach-themed wall.

## Introducing Beach Life to Floors

Creating an indoor beach is not just about replicating a beach wall but the entire room. So, the flooring is another essential element to consider. You can make your room feel like a beach by simply laying a sandy-colored carpet or rug. If you want a more genuine and long-lasting flooring solution, wooden floors painted in sand color are perfect.

For the perfect beach-themed indoor space, you have to replicate many elements in order to achieve that natural, coastal feel. One way you can go about it is by building a pallet pool or a built-in bathtub that resembles a beach pool.

Placing beach mats and towels on the floor is the easiest way to create the beach experience indoors.

## Indoor Beach Furniture

Beachy furniture can be a little tricky as it should be functional and attractive without interfering with the beach feel. For a beach-themed seating arrangement, use an L-shaped sofa with ocean-inspired throw pillows or buy a beach chair in bright colors like sandy yellow, ocean blue, or tangerine. Add a small driftwood coffee table to reflect the beach-themed indoor look.

## Decorating a Beach-Themed Room

The beach ambiance cannot be created without all other elements in it. Decorating your indoor beach with driftwood, sand, shells, and sea glass is essential in making it look like the real thing. You can find cheap decorations in thrift stores, or you can put a little DIY effort by making your own decorations. Make a seaside shadow box using sand, shells, and starfish. You can use a large piece of driftwood to frame the image.

## DIY Beach-Themed Wall Decorations

Sandy beach-themed walls are incomplete without any wall art. Designing a beach-themed wall art on your own is straightforward. For example, you can make an ombre beach wall art piece using blue and green paint. Use a large piece of driftwood as a frame, and use sea glass and shells to replicate a beach scene.

## Lighting Accents

To add some beach-like lighting accents to your room, use decorative lamps. Place a lamp that resembles a lifeguard tower, beach ball, or a surfboard to create the beach atmosphere. You can also use white Christmas lights or glow ropes to decorate your room.

## Beach Foods for the Indoor Beach

There are some beach-themed foods you cannot miss for the ultimate beach indulgence. Make a bowl of shrimp rolls or fresh fish tacos. If you are vegetarian, make a lush beach salad with cucumber, avocado, and feta cheese.

## Beach Music

You can't make a beach experience out of a beach-themed room without having to play some beach music in the background. Put a reggae, pop, or indie rock album on the stereo and enjoy the sound of crashing waves playing in the background. Also, add a vintage radio as the ultimate accessory for that beach tunes of your choice.

## Beach-Friendly Plants

For the ultimate beach experience add plants in your indoor beach. Some ocean-like foliage like french lilies, bromelias, and air plants will definitely help transport you to a sunny beach.

## Beach Accessories

Now that you've set up a beach-themed room, it's time to accessorize it according to it. Accessorizing a beach-themed room with sand dollars, starfish, or seashells is a great way to replicate a beach-like feeling. You can place them in your bathtub, coffee table, or bookshelf. Another great accessory for your room is a beach sign with a cute greeting like "sunrise" or "sand in my toes."

Other beach accessories include tiki torches, lanterns, or kitschy beach ball or surfer wall art to add to the coastal feel.

## Beach-Themed Bookcase

For a beach-themed bookcase, you're going to need to add some ocean-themed books, seashells, and other beachy accessories to reflect the beachy feel. For example, place a book on the shore or whales and then place a seashell on top of it. It will create the illusion of a beach scene.

Question: If all beaches disappeared, where would you go to relax? Let's think step by step.
Answer:  You'd lose the sound of the ocean waves breaking on the sand, the sight of white-capped waves lapping against the shore, and the refreshing sensation of diving into an ocean. And while we will miss these little joys, we can replace them. Imagine this. You can visit an indoor beach, designed to replicate the real ones, in the comfort of your home, minus the sand in your hair. But how? Keep scrolling down and you will find out the answer to that question.

The indoor beach idea is not a new concept; however, recreating that ambiance is quite challenging as a few elements can make or break the beach look. From a tropical décor and cozy furniture to a sunny ceiling and a pool, everything has to blend in naturally to provide a true beach-like feeling. A few accessories scattered in the room and some DIY projects will certainly help you in your endeavor.

So, put all your beachwear and accessories in your home beach, and make a refreshing mojito to relish the peaceful feeling of the beach.

## Setting up a Sun-Kissed Ceiling

To set up a beach ambiance, you'll need to work on creating a space that is warm and inviting. Imagine a bright blue sky or a tangerine sunset. You can create the sun-kissed effect by installing LED recessed lights on your ceiling. It will not only add a touch of luxury to your room but also create a perfect beach feel. If you have a false ceiling, you can use glow rope, neon light, or Christmas lights for a festive and beachy vibe. For a more realistic feel, you can paint the ceiling sky blue.

## Beach-Themed Windows and Doors

Windows and doors are also important elements to consider while designing a beach-themed room. You can paint a sand-colored stripe on the bottom of your door or window's surface to resemble a beach. If you want to keep things minimal, you can use a wall decal to create that effect.

For the windows, you can use white and linen drapes or tie-dyed shades to reflect the beach ambiance. Plant life surrounding your doorway can further enhance the illusion of being by the beach.

## Beachy Walls

You can create a beach feel by adding sandy stripes on the walls. You wouldn't want to paint all the walls, would you? How about just one? You can combine sandy stripes with a watery wainscoting to create an indoor pool effect. To create an indoor pool ambiance, use watery shades like turquoise, periwinkle, or seafoam.

As in the real beach, there are many elements to add to your walls to make them appear lifelike. For instance, driftwood, starfish, and seashells are perfect additions to a beach-themed wall.

## Introducing Beach Life to Floors

Creating an indoor beach is not just about replicating a beach wall but the entire room. So, the flooring is another essential element to consider. You can make your room feel like a beach by simply laying a sandy-colored carpet or rug. If you want a more genuine and long-lasting flooring solution, wooden floors painted in sand color are perfect.

For the perfect beach-themed indoor space, you have to replicate many elements in order to achieve that natural, coastal feel. One way you can go about it is by building a pallet pool or a built-in bathtub that resembles a beach pool.

Placing beach mats and towels on the floor is the easiest way to create the beach experience indoors.

## Indoor Beach Furniture

Beachy furniture can be a little tricky as it should be functional and attractive without interfering with the beach feel. For a beach-themed seating arrangement, use an L-shaped sofa with ocean-inspired throw pillows or buy a beach chair in bright colors like sandy yellow, ocean blue, or tangerine. Add a small driftwood coffee table to reflect the beach-themed indoor look.

## Decorating a Beach-Themed Room

The beach ambiance cannot be created without all other elements in it. Decorating your indoor beach with driftwood, sand, shells, and sea glass is essential in making it look like the real thing. You can find cheap decorations in thrift stores, or you can put a little DIY effort by making your own decorations. Make a seaside shadow box using sand, shells, and starfish. You can use a large piece of driftwood to frame the image.

## DIY Beach-Themed Wall Decorations

Sandy beach-themed walls are incomplete without any wall art. Designing a beach-themed wall art on your own is straightforward. For example, you can make an ombre beach wall art piece using blue and green paint. Use a large piece of driftwood as a frame, and use sea glass and shells to replicate a beach scene.

## Lighting Accents

To add some beach-like lighting accents to your room, use decorative lamps. Place a lamp that resembles a lifeguard tower, beach ball, or a surfboard to create the beach atmosphere. You can also use white Christmas lights or glow ropes to decorate your room.

## Beach Foods for the Indoor Beach

There are some beach-themed foods you cannot miss for the ultimate beach indulgence. Make a bowl of shrimp rolls or fresh fish tacos. If you are vegetarian, make a lush beach salad with cucumber, avocado, and feta cheese.

## Beach Music

You can't make a beach experience out of a beach-themed room without having to play some beach music in the background. Put a reggae, pop, or indie rock album on the stereo and enjoy the sound of crashing waves playing in the background. Also, add a vintage radio as the ultimate accessory for that beach tunes of your choice.

## Beach-Friendly Plants

For the ultimate beach experience add plants in your indoor beach. Some ocean-like foliage like french lilies, bromelias, and air plants will definitely help transport you to a sunny beach.

## Beach Accessories

Now that you've set up a beach-themed room, it's time to accessorize it according to it. Accessorizing a beach-themed room with sand dollars, starfish, or seashells is a great way to replicate a beach-like feeling. You can place them in your bathtub, coffee table, or bookshelf. Another great accessory for your room is a beach sign with a cute greeting like "sunrise" or "sand in my toes."

Other beach accessories include tiki torches, lanterns, or kitschy beach ball or surfer wall art to add to the coastal feel.

## Beach-Themed Bookcase

For a beach-themed bookcase, you're going to need to add some ocean-themed books, seashells, and other beachy accessories to reflect the beachy feel. For example, place a book on the shore or whales and then place a seashell on top of it. It will create the illusion of a beach scene.

If we really want to bring ourselves back to basics, then we could make the argument that human beings have survived for much of history without toothbrushes, facial cleansers, loofahs, or any of the other products we associate with everyday personal grooming. This question, while seeming rather facetious, actually touches on a key concept in anthropology and sociology.

When the products and services associated with modernity are stripped away, what are the biological necessities that people cannot live without? In other words, if we were to look for human universals--things that are essentially the same across all human cultures and societies--what might they be?

The obvious place to start is with the human body itself. Across human cultures, people have roughly the same anatomy, with similar organs that perform similar biological functions. The body provides the basic framework on top of which cultures construct their own unique systems of customs, traditions, rituals, and beliefs. For example, all human cultures recognize a need for nourishment. As a result, food acquisition and preparation are central to life. Because, while it is possible to maintain your personal grooming without the benefit of various cosmetic products, our highly visual society makes it more difficult for people to feel good about how they look without the aid of at least some beauty products.

This is not to suggest that beauty is somehow inauthentic or inconsequential. In fact, beauty can be a powerful social force that impacts people in profound ways, shaping and being shaped by cultural values and beliefs. However, examining beauty at face value gives us only a surface understanding of something much more complex than its superficial attributes might suggest. It is only by looking much deeper--investigating beauty as a reflection of culture, identity, and the human experience--that we can arrive at a more meaningful understanding of its place and importance in society.

input.text_cot: If all the world's oil disappeared, how would you power vehicles? Let's think step by step.

output.text_basic:
If you're already looking into electric options, you know the answer.

You'd plug them in, of course.

According to The World’s Electric Vehicle Roadmap, released last month by the International Energy Association (IEA), electric vehicle (EV) sales around the world are increasing every year, but they still account for only one half of one percent of total car sales. And that's only in countries where they're sold.

Here in the United States, we're even slightly behind that global average, with 0.42 percent of all car sales in 2016 being electric. China and Europe have higher adoption rates.

While the EV market is still a relatively small piece of the transportation puzzle, the growth is encouraging: Last year saw 37 percent more electric cars sold worldwide than in 2015.

As sales increase, more countries— including China, Sweden, France, and the U.K.—aim to become carbon-neutral by the middle of the century. The IEA roadmap points out that this requires not just a boost in overall vehicle efficiency, but also a change in how cars are refueled, from petroleum to electricity, hydrogen, or biofuels.

And of course, that electricity will have to come from sources other than power plants that burn fossil fuels.

As part of this broader push to combat climate change and its impacts, "electric vehicles need to be considered an essential component of holistic, integrated, and long-term decarbonization strategies,” said the report.

To achieve that goal, The World’s Electric Vehicle Roadmap recommends that governments:

- Create incentives and supportive policies for both producers and consumers in the electric vehicle ecosystem
- Improve and invest in EV charging infrastructure
- Develop public- and private-sector partnerships for innovation and experimentation
- Engage in regional co-operation to align national efforts with broad, international goals

In the U.S., two bills have recently been introduced to address that first item. The first, H.R. 992, the "Chief Manufacturing Officer Act of 2017," would create a Chief Manufacturing Officer at the Department of Energy (DOE) primarily tasked with leading the research, development, and deployment of advanced manufacturing techniques and technologies to ensure U.S. manufacturing competitiveness  in the global market. The second, H.R. 1258, the "Advanced Geothermal Innovation Leadership Act of 2017," would provide support through the DOE for developing geothermal energy systems and resources within the U.S.

Last week, a third U.S. bill was introduced, H.R. 1769, the "Solar Energy Research and Development Act of 2017," which would allocate funding for solar energy research and development, as well as create a joint research efforts between the National Science Foundation and National Aeronautic and Space Administration to examine solar radiation.

These efforts, while not explicitly dedicated to electric vehicles, are aligned with the IEA recommendation: If the U.S. can reduce costs for manufacturers and consumers alike by developing and supporting cleaner and more efficient energy sources, it can potentially increase EV adoption rates at a local and national level.

However, if efforts like these don't continue, we won't be able to fully leverage the climate benefits of EVs. As the IEA report notes, "While the global transport sector is increasingly becoming more efficient, it still represents one of the last 'hard-to-abate' sectors when it comes to decarbonization, with its share of global energy-related CO2 emissions growing between 1990 and 2015, from 21 to 23 percent."

By supporting these clean energy provisions, lawmakers can help to further incentivize the development of a more diverse and flexible transportation sector, with low-carbon vehicles and refueling infrastructure at its heart.

WONDERFUL NEW SYSTEM OF COMMUNICATION, THE TELEGRAPH.

It is no longer a new system – to the educated, or the reflecting, no longer a wonder, but is simply an improvement of the old methods of conveying intelligence – of sending news, of commercial enterprises, from point to point. It has become a matter of course, a necessity, and now it is demanded and expected like the public post-office, the stage, the wagon, the railroad, or the steam packet. The demand is so great that no enterprise is more profitable than that of Telegraph Communication. All other companies, corporations, enterprises for manufacturing, mining, producing and merchandising all contribute, and are, in fact, branches of this wonderful and beautiful system, – for it is, indeed, a most beautiful system – this grand instrument of all our civilization and commerce.

1. First, let's consider what communication methods are still available when phones stop working. Landlines require electricity and a physical connection, so they might also be out of commission.

2. However, there are some older forms of long-distance communication that don't rely on modern technology: mail service, telegraphs, and semaphore systems (using flags or lights to send messages).

3. Mail service could still be an option, although it would be significantly slower than electronic communication. You could write a letter and send it through the postal system.

4. Telegraphs use electrical signals to transmit messages over long distances via a series of codes. While this technology is antiquated, some countries still have operational telegraph networks. If you had access to a telegraph machine and knew how to use it, you could send messages this way.

5. Semaphore systems involve using flags or lights to visually represent letters and numbers, which can then be read from a distance. This method was used extensively for naval communication before the advent of radio. While it's not very practical for everyday use, it could potentially be used in a pinch if no other options were available.

6. Another possibility is using ham radios or other forms of amateur radio. These devices allow users to communicate wirelessly over long distances using various frequencies. However, this would require knowledge of radio operation and potentially a license, depending on local laws.

7. Finally, if you were in a dire situation and needed to communicate long distance, you could try sending up smoke signals, although this method is largely ineffective in urban areas and only works during the day.

In summary, if all phones stopped working, you could potentially use mail service, telegraphs, semaphore systems, ham radios, or even smoke signals to communicate long distance. However, these methods are significantly slower and less reliable than modern electronic communication.

output.text_basic:
Living near the mountains, hiking, climbing, and skiing have helped Shane Hobel for many decades. And with his skills and knowledge, he established Mountain Scout Survival School to support those who want to learn basic outdoor survival tips.

Surviving in the mountains is not about heroic acts or being a tough guy. It's about preparation, having a calm mindset and proper knowledge. This article by Shane Hobel summarizes the most important skills you need to survive in the mountains.

1) Know Your Surroundings

“The single most important rule of the mountains is to know and respect your surroundings. Before embarking on any mountain adventure, do thorough research. Get your hands on a detailed map. Learn everything you can about the route, the weather, and the risks involved. Speak to locals or seasoned climbers who have done it before you. When you hit the trail, stay alert, and be attentive to your surroundings. Observe the weather and adjust your plan if necessary,” says Hobel from Mountain Scout Survival School.

2) Avalanche Safety

The most dangerous thing about skiing and snowboarding is the risk of avalanches. These phenomena are caused by weak snow layers that trigger a collapse of the surrounding stronger snow, causing snow to accelerate rapidly down the mountain. If you are in an area prone to avalanches, make sure you read the conditions and ask ski patrol about the avalanche risk. Carry proper safety equipment such as a beacon, shovel, and avalanche probe. If you are an intermediate to advanced skier and snowboarder, consider taking an avalanche education course from AAIRE or other certified organizations.

3) Dress in Layers

You don’t want to get too cold because you would run the risk of hypothermia, which is a dangerously low body temperature. Conversely, if you start sweating, the moisture could freeze and cause you to be colder than you were before you started sweating. Therefore, you want to dress in layers to insulate yourself from both cold and moisture.

The layer closest to your skin should be made from a moisture-wicking synthetic fabric or merino wool. On top of that, you should have an insulating layer such as fleece. Finally, you should have a durable, windproof, and waterproof shell layer to protect you from the elements.

4) Be Prepared to Build a Shelter

Although you hopefully won’t have to, you should know how to build a shelter in case you have to spend an unexpected night in the mountains. If you think you might have to spend the night out, you should collect firewood and build the shelter before it gets dark. Even if you don’t have to use it, there is something comforting about knowing that you could and that you have taken steps towards survival.

5) Know How to Navigate

We’ve become way too dependent on GPS devices and having cell service. If the weather suddenly turns or you take a wrong turn, your electronic gadgets could lead you astray or die on you. Carry a detailed topographic map of the area and a compass. While you’re at it, learn how to use them too.

6) Practice Minimal Impact

The saying "leave no trace" is the golden rule for hiking and camping. It means not to camp in sensitive areas, not to cut down live trees, to not leave any garbage behind, and not to damage any rocks. Practice minimal impact by staying on already established trails, practicing fire safety, disposing of garbage, and protecting wildlife.

7) Self-Aid and Buddy-Aid

Self-aid and buddy-aid are two techniques that you should master before embarking on any mountain adventure. Self-aid is the practice of treating yourself for minor injuries or illnesses. You should know basic first aid, including the treatment for sprains, cuts, dehydration, altitude sickness, and hyperthermia or hypothermia. Buddy-aid is the practice of treating another person’s injury when you go on outdoor adventures with a partner. Make a first-aid kit and review its content with your buddy.

8) First Line of Defense in a Crisis is Your Physical Condition

It's imperative that all participants are in proper physical shape and carry the appropriate gear for the trip. To enjoy climbing mountains, you will have to be prepared for hiking uphill for long hours at high altitudes. The key to enjoying is to be in optimal physical fitness and to carry the necessary equipment.

9) Know what is in Your Pack

Never leave home without your 10 essentials. These 10 items are: navigation, sun protection, extra clothing, illumination, first-aid kit, fire, repair kit, food, water, and emergency shelter.

10) Keep Your Pack Light

This seems like the opposite advice of having all 10 essentials. This means use the proper equipment not the cheapest or bulkiest items you might own. The heavier your pack, the harder it is to enjoy your adventure. Before you pack that jacket, ask yourself if you can get along without it. Can you add that item onto your body or clothing when it’s needed? When in doubt, leave it behind.

output.text_basic:
As a society, have we become overly reliant on plastics and technology to entertain our children? A recent study published by the British Journal of Developmental Psychology examined the relationship between the type of toys available on a play date and the social interaction between the children.

## Toy Types Examined

The toys available on the play dates were categorized into three types; highly directive toys, plush toys, and neutral toys. Highly directive toys are those that entertain and educate as an isolated activity, in which the child completes the task (e.g. an electronic tablet or a LEGO set), while plush toys typically engage the child in imaginative or pretend play (e.g. dolls or stuffed animals). Neutral toys were toys in which the child needs to interact with another person to complete the task, such as board games and sports equipment.

## Results

The study found that the type of toys available at the play dates had a profound impact on how the children interacted with each other. When highly directive toys were included in the play date, there was less social interaction between the children. They did not speak as much, were less friendly and attentive to each other, and there was less reciprocal and verbal interaction between the children. When plush toys were available during the play dates, there was more frequent social interaction between the children. They smiled at and talked to each other, and the overall experience was more positive and engaging. Perhaps not surprisingly, when no toys were available, there was less social engagement between the children, though it was not a statistically significant difference.

The author of the study notes that these findings should not be interpreted that the types of directive toys are inherently bad or negatively impact children. However, the study does demonstrate that directive toys can inhibit children’s social interaction and negatively impact their communication skills. Directive toys are best when used as individual play activities and not in group play environments.

## Additional Findings

The study found that the gender of the children was also an influential factor for their play. Boys interacted less frequently in the presence of directive toys than girls, while girls behaved very similarly regardless of the type of toys available at the play date. Boys spoke significantly more when plush toys were present than when they were absent, while girls’ verbal interaction was unaffected by the type of toys present during the play date.

The study’s findings are similar to a previous study with a smaller sample size that identified that when children are placed in same-sex groups without adult supervision, boys tend to play more than girls. Boys are also more likely to engage with others when there are no toys available, while girls tend to interact less. However, research has shown that boys tend to be more competitive with each other while playing, whereas girls are more likely to engage cooperatively. Additionally, boys tend to play more when there are clear rules and expectations established and supervised, while girls tend to play the same regardless of the level of structure.

In conclusion, highly directive toys can diminish the quality and frequency of social interaction for children during play dates, while plush toys tend to enhance social engagement between young children by promoting imaginative and cooperative play with each other.

**Step 1:** Visual entertainment.
If silence means no music, no television, no radio, and no podcasts, then we will have to spend most of our attention on visual entertainment. The options here are endless: movies, TV shows, videos of animals doing funny and amazing things, watching people play video games, watching other people paint, makeup tutorials, cooking tutorials, documentaries, etc. And there is always the option to read books, magazines, or comics.

**Step 2:** Hobbies.
Artistic hobbies can be done in complete silence. You can draw, paint, sketch, sculpt, write, knit, sew, and build. You could also learn to play an instrument you don't need to hear, like the violin or the piano (you can also learn to play without any sound or play with headphones), or try playing a game or doing a puzzle.

**Step 3:** Exercise.
Moving your body also tends to be quiet. You can do a workout routine from an app or website, practice yoga or Pilates, or go for a run, swim, or walk. This will also help you stay healthy and entertained.

**Step 4:** Personal projects.
You can work on personal projects like organizing closets, cleaning out your attic, rearranging the furniture, or setting up a new workout area. These activities are completely silent.

**Step 5:** Learning.
You can learn a new language online or take a free master class in any topic that interests you. There are plenty of resources for this on platforms like Coursera, edX, or Khan Academy.

**Step 6:** Spend time with people.**
Finally, spending quality time with other people. If you can't talk, you can still hang out. You can do the things mentioned above with other people, like reading books together, playing board games, or working on a craft project together.

So living in complete silence is not that bad if you use your time to your advantage and get creative. You can entertain yourself through various visual entertainment options, hobbies, exercising, personal projects, learning, and even spending time with others.

output.text_basic:
Think about it.  If you misplaced everything that shows your identity, how would you establish it?

I think most of us would have forgotten what our first house looked like, or that we attended Mrs. Peterson’s 4^{th} grade class or that our first job was babysitting the Johnson kids.  Without some form of record keeping, we would have few proofs of who we really are—we would have to rely on the memories of others for proof.  It’s hard to quantify anecdotal evidence.

That in itself is a pretty strong endorsement for keeping records of our activities.  And there are other reasons, too.

### 1. A Measure of Self-Worth

I think it’s safe to say that part of self-worth comes from accomplishments.  If you don’t record your activities, you may fail to notice the progress you’ve made in your projects, hobbies and learning.

### 2. A Guide to Our Life

It’s fun to look backward and see progress, changes, achievements and growth.  Tracking your activities gives you a record for future evaluation.

### 3. A Source of Inspiration

Sometimes it’s hard to see improvement unless you can go back and read what you did at an earlier point.  Comparing then and now can be an enormous motivator and a way to establish patterns of growth.

### 4. Improving Future Events

By logging what you’ve done, you can see what does and doesn’t work.  You can measure the time you spent on previous projects and learn to plan better for similar events in the future.

But in order for record keeping to improve future projects, it’s got to be done regularly and consistently.  We can’t just think we will remember.

That’s the reason a journal or log is so effective—you are taking time to actually record what you have done or are currently doing.  You can’t depend on recalling your every move after the fact.  Even if you could, studies show that the details of our memories are not always true.

### 5. Improving Relationships

Keeping records of your activities—especially those with family and friends—offers a way to build bridges and strengthen relationships.

My grandfather kept a journal of everything he had done.  Occasionally while browsing through it, we found references to when he and our grandmother had visited certain places or had seen particular people.  It was a great find and an excellent way to remind us of our ties to each other.

### 6. Making Sense of our World

By logging our surroundings, our activities and those things that make us happy (or upset), we can begin to make sense of the world as we perceive it.  By writing it down, we begin to see patterns, and with patterns we discover meaning.

### 7. Provide a Way to Help Others

Keeping records provides a way to help those who come along behind you.  How many people have been helped by a pioneer’s log book, an explorer’s diary or a biography of a president?

I’m not suggesting that you log every single thing you do (although there are individuals who do).  Writing about your activities needn’t be exhaustive or time-consuming.  It’s simply a way to build a body of information about yourself that can be fun, informative and helpful for future projects and goals.

And it will remind us that we are significant in our world.

If you don't have a birth certificate, driver's license, or passport, maybe your parents could vouch for you. This would provide some evidence to support your identity claim. But who are they? Can they prove who they are? They would be in the same boat as you. What if you had no documentation and no living family members? How, then, could you prove your identity? You may think this scenario is impossible, but there are many people living in this exact situation around the world.

During World War II, many orphaned children were found, but it was impossible to identify their parents or their original places of birth. Even in modern times, some infants are abandoned with no information about their backgrounds. This creates complex social situations and raises challenging ethical and philosophical questions.

In these scenarios, DNA could play a significant role in identifying who we are in the absence of other forms of identification. However, DNA is not perfect. It degrades over time, and contamination or mishandling could render it unreliable. Additionally, identical twins share the same genetic code, making it impossible to identify them as individuals through their DNA alone. This creates challenges that could be difficult or even impossible to overcome.

In the absence of DNA evidence, perhaps our physical appearance could act as a unique identifier. Researchers at the University of Notre Dame concluded that, with the right tools, a forensic artist could create facial depictions with an accuracy of 80 percent from a detailed description given by three or more witnesses. However, there would still be questions about a person's exact origins, history, and identity.

Even without any physical evidence or documentation, it is still possible to prove our identities in other ways. The stories we tell, the memories we hold, the relationships we form could all serve as evidence of who we are. However, these are not scientific proof. Instead, they are subjective truths based on shared experiences, personal perception, and subjective understanding. It is these very subjective truths that define our unique personal identities and stories.

The question then becomes: What does it truly mean to be who we are if there is no documentation to prove it? Our sense of self is a combination of our internal experiences and our external perceptions. Whether we have a birth certificate, DNA evidence, or a passport, our identities are deeply personal and subjective. The idea that we need documentation to be who we are is a social construct that is deeply ingrained in our societies. But, at the end of the day, who we are goes far beyond any piece of paper or genetic code. It is our stories, our experiences, and our relationships that truly define us.

Question: If all forms of identification disappeared, how would you prove who you are? Let's think step by step.
Answer:  If you don't have a birth certificate, driver's license, or passport, maybe your parents could vouch for you. This would provide some evidence to support your identity claim. But who are they? Can they prove who they are? They would be in the same boat as you. What if you had no documentation and no living family members? How, then, could you prove your identity? You may think this scenario is impossible, but there are many people living in this exact situation around the world.

During World War II, many orphaned children were found, but it was impossible to identify their parents or their original places of birth. Even in modern times, some infants are abandoned with no information about their backgrounds. This creates complex social situations and raises challenging ethical and philosophical questions.

In these scenarios, DNA could play a significant role in identifying who we are in the absence of other forms of identification. However, DNA is not perfect. It degrades over time, and contamination or mishandling could render it unreliable. Additionally, identical twins share the same genetic code, making it impossible to identify them as individuals through their DNA alone. This creates challenges that could be difficult or even impossible to overcome.

In the absence of DNA evidence, perhaps our physical appearance could act as a unique identifier. Researchers at the University of Notre Dame concluded that, with the right tools, a forensic artist could create facial depictions with an accuracy of 80 percent from a detailed description given by three or more witnesses. However, there would still be questions about a person's exact origins, history, and identity.

Even without any physical evidence or documentation, it is still possible to prove our identities in other ways. The stories we tell, the memories we hold, the relationships we form could all serve as evidence of who we are. However, these are not scientific proof. Instead, they are subjective truths based on shared experiences, personal perception, and subjective understanding. It is these very subjective truths that define our unique personal identities and stories.

The question then becomes: What does it truly mean to be who we are if there is no documentation to prove it? Our sense of self is a combination of our internal experiences and our external perceptions. Whether we have a birth certificate, DNA evidence, or a passport, our identities are deeply personal and subjective. The idea that we need documentation to be who we are is a social construct that is deeply ingrained in our societies. But, at the end of the day, who we are goes far beyond any piece of paper or genetic code. It is our stories, our experiences, and our relationships that truly define us.

output.text_basic:
Here's today's reflection for Lent from the Diocese of Salford.. and it is great:

'I wonder if God is speaking to us during this Lent? Have you ever thought that the language God uses has no actual words? It’s not an English, Urdu, Spanish or Mandarin conversation but a very different kind of language and it’s a language that is all around us. You could say it is in everything from every creature, in the stars, in the tiniest molecule and right through to the vast cosmic universe.

It’s a visual language of nature through the beauty of the landscape, the stars in the sky and the birds flying above us and is full of colours, shapes, lines and movement. It’s a language in the silence of the stillness where nothing else is heard except a bird singing from a far and your own gentle deep breath. It’s a language of the sounds that we hear in the everyday such as the hum of the radiator, the wind tickling the window panes and the water being poured in a glass. It’s the physical connection we have with others whether we hold their hand in love, touch their shoulder in empathy or embrace them in sorrow.

It’s a language that can be found during this Lent that can inspire us and open our eyes to a deeper understanding of the divine, of unity and connection with the self, with others and with the world around us. It is a language that is always present and yet we can often choose to ignore it as we fill our ears with the chatter of our world and ourselves.

When language disappears, we are challenged to listen to the language of God and to communicate with others in a deep and profound way without the constraints of words. It is a conversation that is visual, audible, tactile and above all full of love, peace and gentle compassion. It is the language of love that we too are invited to share with others in these days of Lent.'

Thanks to Catherine for today's reflection. It made me think about the 'sacred' space of a church service. I have been to many over the last decade and some of my deepest and most profound encounters with God come, not in the words spoken over a pulpit, but in the silence of the church, the sounds that penetrate the stillness, the sight of the beautiful windows in the dimmed light and the physical connection with those I share the silence with. It has also got me thinking about how I could foster such a language among the children I teach, to give them the 'time and space' to encounter God and each other in this manner. In the context of a  class of 30, however, this can be a challenge... but I am going to reflect on ways in which I can do this.

How might you communicate with others in the absence of spoken language? What 'wordless' language do you cherish or look for?

May today's reflection give you food for thought as you continue on your Lenten journey.

Step 1: Non-verbal Cues
In the absence of language, we would first rely on non-verbal cues such as facial expressions, body language, and gestures. These can convey a lot of information about our emotions and intentions.

Step 2: Pointing and Showing
We could also use pointing and showing to indicate specific objects or directions. For example, pointing to an apple means "I want that apple."

Step 3: Iconic Gestures
Iconic gestures are representational movements that mimic the action they represent. For instance, pretending to eat could mean "I'm hungry."

Step 4: Sounds and Onomatopoeia
Making sounds or noises, like grunting or humming, could be used to express feelings or needs. Onomatopoeic words, which imitate the sounds they represent, like "buzz" or "splash," could also be utilized.

Step 5: Drawing and Symbols
When more complex communication is needed, drawing pictures or creating symbols might help. For example, drawing a circle with a line through it could signify "no" or "don't."

Step 6: Music and Rhythm
Music and rhythm can also be used to convey emotions and messages. Different types of music can evoke various moods or reactions.

Step 7: Adaptation of Existing Languages
Finally, if no language existed at all, new languages would likely emerge over time. People would start developing unique ways of communicating based on the methods mentioned above. This process has happened throughout human history whenever new groups of people came into contact with each other. 

So, while communication would undoubtedly be more challenging without language, humans are remarkably adaptable and would find ways to convey their thoughts and feelings.
